changed_in.5.4: A second argument, `lax`, is added. A true value lifts the limit on what a byte sequence may decode to, accepting anything up to `0x7FFFFFFF`; malformed and overlong sequences are refused either way. The default reading also became stricter at the same time: a sequence encoding a surrogate, `0xD800` through `0xDFFF`, now stops the walk with an error, where earlier versions handed it to the loop like any other character. A string that itself begins in the middle of a character is refused by the call that sets the loop up, where earlier versions accepted that call and raised at the loop's first step instead.
